{
  "code": "`timescale 1ns/1ps\n\n// csr_regblock — memory-mapped control/status register block\n//\n// Four mapped registers decoded combinationally from addr:\n//   0 CTRL        read-write, reset 0, bit 0 is the interrupt enable\n//   1 STATUS      read-only, bit 0 is the sticky event flag\n//   2 EVENT_CLEAR write-1-to-clear on bit 0, reads as zero\n//   3 VERSION     read-only constant 32'h0000_0001\n// Every other address reads as zero and ignores writes.\n//\n// A transaction is any rising clk edge with sel high; ready marks exactly\n// those cycles and rdata presents the addressed value in that same cycle\n// (REQ-INTF-002, REQ-FUNC-002). irq is a plain AND of the sticky flag and\n// CTRL bit 0 so it carries no delay of its own (REQ-TIME-001).\nmodule csr_regblock #(\n    parameter int ADDR_W = 4\n) (\n    input  logic              clk,\n    input  logic              rst_n,\n    input  logic              sel,\n    input  logic              write,\n    input  logic [ADDR_W-1:0] addr,\n    input  logic [31:0]       wdata,\n    input  logic              event_in,\n    output logic [31:0]       rdata,\n    output logic              ready,\n    output logic              irq\n);\n\n    // Register map addresses, sized to the address bus.\n    localparam logic [ADDR_W-1:0] ADDR_CTRL        = ADDR_W'(0);\n    localparam logic [ADDR_W-1:0] ADDR_STATUS      = ADDR_W'(1);\n    localparam logic [ADDR_W-1:0] ADDR_EVENT_CLEAR = ADDR_W'(2);\n    localparam logic [ADDR_W-1:0] ADDR_VERSION     = ADDR_W'(3);\n\n    localparam logic [31:0] VERSION_VALUE = 32'h0000_0001;\n\n    // ADDR_W must be wide enough to decode the four mapped registers.\n    initial if (!(ADDR_W >= 2)) $fatal(1, \"csr_regblock: ADDR_W must be >= 2\");\n\n    // ── State ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    logic [31:0] ctrl_reg;          // CTRL, address 0\n    logic        event_flag;        // STATUS bit 0, sticky\n\n    // ── Address decode (combinational) ───────────────────────────────────\n    logic sel_ctrl, sel_status, sel_event_clear, sel_version;\n    logic addr_mapped;\n\n    // Decode the current address into per-register select lines.\n    always_comb begin\n        sel_ctrl        = (addr == ADDR_CTRL);\n        sel_status      = (addr == ADDR_STATUS);\n        sel_event_clear = (addr == ADDR_EVENT_CLEAR);\n        sel_version     = (addr == ADDR_VERSION);\n        addr_mapped     = sel_ctrl | sel_status | sel_event_clear | sel_version;\n    end\n\n    // Transaction qualifiers for this cycle.\n    logic do_write;\n    logic do_read;\n    assign do_write = sel & write;\n    assign do_read  = sel & ~write;\n\n    // ── CTRL register ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    // Written by a bus write to address 0; cleared by synchronous reset.\n    always_ff @(posedge clk) begin\n        if (!rst_n) begin\n            ctrl_reg <= 32'h0000_0000;\n        end else if (do_write && sel_ctrl) begin\n            ctrl_reg <= wdata;\n        end\n    end\n\n    // ── Sticky event flag ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    // event_in sets the flag on any cycle it is high and wins a\n    // simultaneous write-1-to-clear (REQ-FUNC-007); a write of 1 to\n    // EVENT_CLEAR bit 0 clears it (REQ-FUNC-006).\n    always_ff @(posedge clk) begin\n        if (!rst_n) begin\n            event_flag <= 1'b0;\n        end else if (event_in) begin\n            event_flag <= 1'b1;\n        end else if (do_write && sel_event_clear && wdata[0]) begin\n            event_flag <= 1'b0;\n        end\n    end\n\n    // ── Read data mux ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    // Presents the addressed register in the same cycle as the read;\n    // zero on idle cycles, on EVENT_CLEAR, and on unmapped addresses.\n    always_comb begin\n        rdata = 32'h0000_0000;\n        if (do_read && addr_mapped) begin\n            unique case (1'b1)\n                sel_ctrl:        rdata = ctrl_reg;\n                sel_status:      rdata = {31'h0, event_flag};\n                sel_event_clear: rdata = 32'h0000_0000;\n                sel_version:     rdata = VERSION_VALUE;\n                default:         rdata = 32'h0000_0000;\n            endcase\n        end\n    end\n\n    // ── Transaction acknowledge ──────────────────────────────────────────\n    // High for exactly the cycles in which sel is high (REQ-INTF-002).\n    assign ready = sel;\n\n    // ── Interrupt request ────────────────────────────────────────────────\n    // Same-cycle function of the sticky flag and the interrupt enable; no\n    // register of its own, so irq never lags its sources (REQ-TIME-001).\n    assign irq = event_flag & ctrl_reg[0];\n\n`ifdef FORMAL\n    // irq is exactly the conjunction of its two sources, every cycle.\n    always @(posedge clk) begin\n        if (rst_n) begin\n            assert (irq == (event_flag & ctrl_reg[0]));\n        end\n    end\n\n    // ready marks exactly the transaction cycles.\n    always @(posedge clk) begin\n        if (rst_n) begin\n            assert (ready == sel);\n        end\n    end\n\n    // A read of VERSION always presents the constant.\n    always @(posedge clk) begin\n        if (rst_n && do_read && sel_version) begin\n            assert (rdata == 32'h0000_0001);\n        end\n    end\n`endif\n\nendmodule // csr_regblock\n",
  "notes": "irq and rdata are combinational by contract: REQ-TIME-001 requires irq to change in the same cycle as its sources, and REQ-FUNC-002 requires rdata in the cycle sel is high. Only CTRL and the sticky flag hold state (33 bits). event_in is resolved ahead of the write-1-to-clear inside one always_ff, so the priority is structural rather than a race between two blocks. Reads never disturb the flag."
}
